external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: The end user's browser, outside the application's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: Serves the browser and enqueues work rather than performing it inline.
processes.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: Consumes queued jobs and performs the work against the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: Carries jobs from the web application to the worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: Application records and the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: Configuration for the web application, holding its message-queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Both of those config stores hold the credentials the process needs — the web application's queue credentials

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: Configuration for the background worker, holding its database credentials.

data_flows.name: page request
data_flows.description: User's browser makes requests to the application; responses ride the same interaction.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
data_flows.encryption_in_transit: encrypted (marked as the one encrypted link)

data_flows.name: enqueue job
data_flows.description: Application places a job on the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: consume job
data_flows.description: Worker takes jobs off the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_flows.name: read write records
data_flows.description: Worker reads and writes application records and log records.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: Application reads its settings, including queue credentials.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: Worker reads its settings, including database credentials.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: Outside the application's network, where the browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: Internet-facing tier holding the web application and its config.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: Tier behind the web tier holding the queue, the worker, its config and the database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is reachable from the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The browser is stated to reach it across the public internet.
